<linkedin_post>Open access to Wikipedia comes with conditions for reuse and limits on how its systems are accessed. The Wikimedia Foundation has brought both points into its court filing on AI and copyright.

The Foundation argues that AI model training can qualify as fair use when the resulting model is new and different from the copyrighted works used to train it. For systems that retrieve copyrighted content to ground chatbot answers, it argues that companies should follow the source’s licensing requirements.

For Wikipedia content, those requirements include crediting creators and sharing adaptations under the same Creative Commons license. The Foundation also asks companies scraping its projects to stay within public API rate limits or use its Enterprise API.</linkedin_post>
